basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixit ergo Deus, producant aquae reptile animae viventis, et volatile super terram sub'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixit ergo Deus, producant aquae reptile animae viventis, et volatile super terram sub firmamento coeli. Et ne forte, quia sunt aquarum animantia, quae non reptando, sed natando, vel pedibus ambulando incedunt, sunt inter volatilia quae ita pennas habent, ut omni usu volandi careant, putaret quisquam aliquod genus volatilium sive aquatilium animantium in hoc Domini verbo esse praetermissum, vigilanter adjungitur:
